newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Olympia not allowed to resume Sabah gaming.
newsitem.headline: Olympia not allowed to resume Sabah gaming.

text.p: The government of the east Malaysian state of Sabah will not allow a unit of Olympia Industries Bhd to resume its gaming operations in the state, the national Bernama news agency said on Wednesday.

Sabah Chief Minister Yong Teck Lee was quoted by Bernama as saying that the state government would not budge from its decision made a year ago not to renew the business licences of all premises selling lottery tickets that have links with Diriwan Corp Bhd, the Olympia unit.

"We will not take any new decision on the matter as we have already made the decision last year. What we will do is to just keep to the decision," he told reporters after chairing a weekly state Cabinet meeting at the state's capital of Kota Kinabalu.
Yong was commenting on a statement by Olympia on Tuesday that its gaming licence in Sabah has been renewed by the Ministry of Finance, with effect from January 1, 1997.
Olympia, which is 54.7 percent owned by Mycom Bhd, had its gaming licence revoked by the ministry in January last year.
Olympia had appealed against the decision.
Diriwan held the gamimg licence for Lotteries Corp Sdn Bhd which operated about 200 gaming outlets in Sabah before the licence was revoked.
Yong said the state Cabinet discussed the matter on Wednesday and agreed to stick to the decision made a year ago.
"The State Secretary will write to the federal authority to inform it that the state government has not changed its decision made last year," he said.
Olympia officials were not immediately available for comment.
Olympia reported a 35 percent decline in net earnings for the year ended June 30, 1996 to 44.78 million ringgit, which it said was partially due to the loss of the gaming licence.
Shares of Olympia, which were suspended on Monday pending announcement of a proposed acquisition, were last traded at 2.21 ringgit.
